ground_truth.description: `_checkpoint` creates a new epoch with the same timestamp for `increase_amount`, ignoring the new lock in `balanceOfNFT`, reducing voting power.
ground_truth.root_cause: `_checkpoint` creates a new epoch with the same timestamp for `increase_amount`, ignoring the new lock in `balanceOfNFT`, reducing voting power.
ground_truth.attack_scenario: A test locks 500e18, increases by 500e18 in one tx, and shows reduced bribe rewards compared to separate locks.
ground_truth.fix_description: In `_checkpoint`, overwrite the latest point if timestamps match, else append a new one. Status: Mitigation confirmed.

vulnerabilities.explanation: The _checkpoint function creates duplicate points with the same timestamp when create_lock and increase_amount are called in the same transaction. This causes incorrect voting power calculations because the balanceOfNFT function uses historical data that ignores new locks created in the same timestamp, leading to reduced voting power.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: 1. User creates a lock with 500e18 tokens using create_lock 2. Within the same transaction, immediately call increase_amount with another 500e18 3. The _checkpoint function will create two points with identical timestamps 4. When balanceOfNFT calculates voting power, it will use historical data that doesn't account for the increased lock amount 5. Result: lower voting power than expected
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: In the _checkpoint function, when recording the changed point into history, check if the last point has the same timestamp as the current one. If so, overwrite the existing point instead of appending a new one. This ensures uniqueness of timestamps in the historical data.

prediction.overall_explanation: The contract contains a logic error in the _checkpoint function where duplicate points with the same timestamp are created when multiple locking operations occur in a single transaction. This leads to incorrect voting power calculations as the balanceOfNFT function may reference outdated historical data, resulting in reduced voting power for users who perform multiple operations in one transaction.
